Transmute

trans-MYOOT · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To transmute is to change into a different form or substance.

Alchemists once dreamed of a method to transmute common lead into gold.

Worked Example

The therapist encouraged her to transmute her grief into something productive, like the community garden she eventually built.

Transmute describes a fundamental change from one form or substance into something else entirely, whether it's a literal material or an abstract feeling.

How Transmute Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

transform

transform: change completely in form or nature

convert

convert: change from one form to another

Antonyms

preserve

preserve: keep something unchanged

maintain

maintain: keep something in its existing state

How Strong Is It? — adjust → transmute → annihilate

adjust vs. transmute

adjust vs. transmute: Adjusting something is a small tweak; the underlying thing stays fundamentally the same.

annihilate vs. transmute

annihilate vs. transmute: To annihilate something is to destroy it completely, the opposite of transmuting it into something new.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — trans-

prefix — trans-: across, beyond (Latin)

root — mut

root — mut: to change (Latin (mutare))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: trans- ("across") + mut ("to change") + -e = to change across into a different form.

Use the root in a new word: mutation

Use the root in a new word: mutation: The same root gives us "mutation," a change in form, especially a genetic one -- a word you already met earlier in this course.
